notes_for_us: water-body is one row for every kind of water and it cannot say clear, shallow, fast or deep. This prompt asks for exactly two properties of its water — small and clear — and the option holds neither, so both ride on prose that a downstream reader may or may not honour. Water properties are probably worth attributes rather than a second row.

Fish are the subject of a fishing game and the only place to file them is collectible-nodes, which is written for ore and herb patches. They are also live moving animals, which npc-population's 'ambient animals' would cover, so the same content has two homes with different Goes to values and nothing to break the tie.

Every Simulation preset assumes an economy, a plot or a hauling route. A quiet single-activity sim with none of those got Role Sim by elimination, and Role Sim dragged a vehicle road onto a creek bank. The genre's smallest possible member has no preset.

notes: Preset Full Stadium kept whole and topped up with the Field Sport scoring set the prompt names outright: penalty spot, goal mouth and out-of-play detection.
P3 is the players' tunnel, which is an enterable structure off the pitch. Drop it only if the tunnel is meant to be a dressed opening the player never walks through.
P0 + tiered is the crowd stands. The Sports notes warn the height has to be captured or the stadium builds flat.
Only the penalty half of the pitch is in play. The prompt says vertical slice, penalty shootouts only, so the far half exists as dressing rather than playable ground.
The scoreboard has to expand past five kicks for sudden death, which makes it a variable-width surface rather than a fixed graphic.

notes_for_us: A 20 KB brief produced a ten-line map and a sixteen-line mechanics array, and that is the correct outcome — but mechanics as a flat list of the user's own words is not a serviceable handoff for a document this size. The stream receiving it gets a lossy summary written by someone whose job was the map. Step 0 is right that this is not our content; the field it routes to is not built to carry this much of it.

The prompt bans real teams, players, sponsors, kits and tournament branding, and repeats the ban twice. It is a hard constraint on everything the image model draws — banners, flags, badges, kits — and there is no field for it. This is the third prompt in this batch whose most emphatic instruction was a prohibition with nowhere to go.

Two things the prompt names as stadium furniture have no option: the floodlights and the animated net. The net in particular is inside trigger-scoring's geometry but the option's text describes the detection plane, so the visible half of the most important object in the scene is carried only by my rewording of it.

The scale question does not fit this prompt as written. The four bands are furniture, buildings, blocks and coastlines, and a stadium is one building containing furniture-scale objects that matter — the ball, the spot, the line. I reworded the question to the prompt's own subjects rather than reading the generic band list, which the skill tells you to do for options but not for this question.
